closing.reason: What held, run live in pgpm_prv-archive against the head: a timestamptz grid with partition_tz Asia/Kolkata, driven from UTC and from America/New_York with offset-less bounds, with the cell start given with an explicit offset, from SQL,DMY and from Postgres,DMY, ndjson and parquet: every call keyed k.ev_2024010118300000 (the cell's start) and read the same 2 rows. The scheduled path: a 1-second Kolkata grid ticked by pgpm.maintain from a New York, SQL,DMY session wrote 6 ledger rows; for each one the key's stem equals _object_stem of the ledger lo, and the object's rows match the live rows of [lo, hi). A date grid driven from Asia/Tokyo with '2024-01-02' and with '02/01/2024' under SQL,DMY was keyed 2024010200000000 and held both 2 January rows (the base keyed Jan 2 and held the Jan 1 row there). ACC-02 (round 1's V-01) is accepted on its three-tree evidence: it passes on the base, where the regression did not exist; it passes on the head; and it fails on the archive_ndjson_bounds_session_zone mutant. It is a regression guard, not a 'fails on base' acceptance. Other entry points: only the two encoders call archive._object_key, and archive.to_s3 keys by child oid, so it is out of scope. What did not hold. (1) V-01, a regression, Tier 3. The encoders now read the bounds on the grid's clock, but archive._refuse_empty_range (#969) still compares the raw text in the caller's session. So the body's sentence 'archive._refuse_empty_range ... reads the same instant pgpm._native_text does' is no longer true on this head, because the read uses partition_tz and not the session zone. The case: a Kolkata grid, a UTC caller, lo '2024-01-02 18:30:00+00' (the cell's start, with its offset) and hi '2024-01-03' (offset-less). The session reads this range as non-empty. On the grid's clock hi equals lo, so the range is empty. The call is admitted, reads 0 rows, and PUTs an empty object (HTTP 200, no content) at the cell's own key instead of refusing. The base read the session's non-empty range (1 row). The recorded-chunk check still refuses this at a recorded key, so nothing is lost: Tier 3 (acts when it should refuse). (2) V-02, pre-existing in the PR's surface, Tier 3, the issue's own consequence. On a date grid the key is the stem of the lo instant, but the read truncates that instant to its day. A Tokyo caller's '2024-01-02 00:00:00+09' (15:00Z on 1 January) reads the whole 1 January cell and keys it d.ev_2024010115000000, a key no cell starts at, while a tick keys it 2024010100000000. That breaks the body's guarantee 'the stem of the instant the call's range read began at' from any TimeZone. The same holds for any offset-less non-midnight lo, from any zone. No open issue names either mechanism: #1030 covers other archive paths and the #969 advice text, and #769 covers a date grid's non-midnight anchor, not a direct call's bound. The new mutations and ACC-02 discriminate as reported.
